title: Unique New York
subtitle: N, Y & Long U
description: This exercise trains the /njuː/ cluster and the palatal glide /j/ (Y-sound), which English learners often drop or distort. Repeating 'unique New York' at speed forces precise articulation of the N-Y transition.
tip: In words like 'new' and 'unique', the /j/ glide is hidden before the /uː/ vowel. Say 'nyoo' not 'noo' — let your tongue briefly touch the palate for the Y before releasing into the vowel.
phrases: You know New York, you need New York, you know you need unique New York.
New York is uniquely unified yet undeniably new.
The youthful new student knew the nuances of unusual university rules.
You use yew wood to create unique new furniture.
Ninety-nine neurons noted the new neural network's unusual nuance.
